title: An element cannot be split into a simpler substance by a chemical change
summary: An element is one kind of atom, and a chemical change does not break it into a simpler substance.
body: OpenStax Chemistry calls a pure substance that chemical changes cannot break into simpler substances an element. Iron, silver, gold, aluminum, sulfur, oxygen, and copper are the everyday examples on the page. It says a bit more than a hundred elements are known, about ninety of them occur on Earth, and about two dozen have been made in laboratories. Those counts are the textbook's, not a new census. A compound, which can be broken down, is a different card.
